sourceAgencies: NJ Division of Pensions and Benefits (SHBP / SEHBP)
Township of Parsippany-Troy Hills Adopted Budget & PBA/Teamsters Contracts
Parsippany-Troy Hills School District User-Friendly Budget (PTHEA Contract)

overview.percentageOfCombinedBudgets: 23.0% of all Parsippany municipal and school spending ($64.5M of $280.2M) goes directly to employee health insurance, pensions, and retirement benefits

healthcarePlans.providers: Horizon Blue Cross Blue Shield / SEHBP (School District) & Township Health Benefits Program

primaryPlans.planName: NJ Educators Health Plan (NJEHP / Chapter 44) & Garden State Health Plan
primaryPlans.description: Enacted under P.L. 2020, c. 44. Caps teacher and school staff premium contributions at 1.7% to 7.2% of salary rather than percentage of premium, shifting double-digit healthcare inflation directly onto Parsippany property taxpayers.
Nationwide PPO network with $10-$15 primary care copays and low out-of-network deductibles for grandfathered and municipal bargaining units.
Covers brand, generic, and high-cost GLP-1/specialty biologics with low employee copays; taxpayers absorb the remaining 85%+ formulary cost.
Employer-paid family dental and optical benefits for eligible full-time township and school employees.

rules.tier: Township Police & Municipal Staff (Chapter 78 / CBA Grid)
rules.employeeContribution: 10.0% to 35.0% of premium based on salary tier
rules.taxpayerContribution: 65.0% to 90.0% of total premium ($22,500 - $29,000/yr per family)
rules.note: For a police officer or supervisor with a $36,000 family health plan, Parsippany taxpayers subsidize ~$23,400+ every year.
Because employee contributions are tied to salary rather than premium growth, 100% of annual health insurance rate hikes fall on the PTHSD school tax levy.

retirementAndLeaveBenefits.taxpayerImpact: Multi-million dollar annual retiree medical expenditure
retirementAndLeaveBenefits.details: Eligible employees retiring after 25 years of pensionable service receive township- or state-paid medical coverage in retirement plus Medicare Part B reimbursements.

retirementAndLeaveBenefits.benefitName: Statutory Pension Systems: Police & Firemen's Retirement System (PFRS) & PERS
retirementAndLeaveBenefits.legalAuthority: NJ Division of Pensions and Benefits
retirementAndLeaveBenefits.details: Mandatory annual municipal employer contributions to Police & Firemen's Retirement System (PFRS) for sworn Parsippany police officers and Public Employees' Retirement System (PERS) for civilian township employees. School teachers belong to TPAF (state-funded employer portion).

retirementAndLeaveBenefits.taxpayerImpact: Lump-sum retirement cash-outs funded via municipal & school reserves
retirementAndLeaveBenefits.details: Veteran employees hired prior to the 2010 statutory reform retain grandfathered contractual rights to cash out accumulated unused sick and vacation days upon retirement.
